applicableAreas: southern portion of site near Valley View Road right-of-way
findings.comment: Buildings are proposed in proximity to existing overhead electric lines shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9). No building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations are provided to verify that the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained between the outside conductor and the nearest building edge.

applicableAreas: buildings 7 and 8 near southern property boundary with overhead lines
findings.comment: Customer facilities (buildings) are proposed near existing overhead electric lines. Radial clearance from the outside conductor to buildings must be verified as minimum 15 feet. No dimension data or clearance analysis is provided to confirm compliance with this radial clearance envelope.

applicableAreas: building roofs and projections on southern buildings
findings.comment: Building projections including roofs, eaves, and overhangs must maintain required clearances from overhead electric conductors. No building elevation sheets showing projections and clearance dimensions from outside conductors are provided.

applicableAreas: buildings near right-of-way with overhead electric lines
findings.comment: Buildings proposed near Valley View Road right-of-way where overhead electric facilities exist. Clearances of 7.5 feet sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial from outside conductors must be maintained as permanent requirements. No surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimensions are provided to verify compliance.

applicableAreas: all buildings near overhead electric lines
findings.comment: No building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are provided in the site plan. Building elevations showing the surveyed location and elevation of overhead electric conductors, performed by a registered surveyor, are required to demonstrate that required clearances are met.

applicableAreas: buildings and building projections on site plan
findings.comment: Section views and enlarged plan detail exhibits showing dimension lines from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and building projections are not provided. These clearance verification exhibits are required to document compliance with 7.5-foot and 15-foot clearance envelopes.

applicableAreas: perimeter fence locations on site plan
findings.comment: Fences are shown on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) adjacent to property boundaries with overhead electric poles and lines in the right-of-way. No dimension annotations showing clearance from the outside conductor to the fence face are provided to verify the minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement.

applicableAreas: fence locations near existing electric poles in right-of-way
findings.comment: Existing electric utility poles are located at property corners in the right-of-way (Sheet 4 and 9). Proposed perimeter fences must maintain minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from pole locations. No dimension data verifying this clearance is provided.

Proposed driveways and parking areas are shown on the grading plan (Sheet 11) in a location that may be in proximity to the overhead electric lines shown on the site plan (Sheet 9). Minimum vertical clearances of 16 feet (parking without truck traffic) or 18 feet (with truck traffic) must be maintained from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities. No mid-span clearance survey data or vertical clearance dimensions from the finished driveway grade to the overhead conductors are provided.

Parking areas are proposed on the site plan. Where vehicles are parked beneath overhead electric lines, minimum vertical clearance must be maintained and documented with clearance dimensions and a site plan note. No such clearance verification or note is provided.

Where clearance dimensions are required and shown on plans, they must be measured from the outside (outermost) conductor, not from the utility pole centerline. No clearance dimensions are provided on the site plan to evaluate; if such dimensions are added, verify they originate from the conductor location and not the pole center.

Water meters are shown on the utility plan (Sheet 19). If any water meter is located within potential clearance distance of overhead electric service drop conductors, minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance must be verified with dimension annotations. No clearance dimensions are provided.

applicableAreas: driveways and parking areas near overhead lines
findings.comment: Proposed site features (driveways, parking) appear to be in proximity to overhead electric lines shown on the site plan. When vertical clearance from overhead facilities to proposed site features appears marginal or insufficient, a registered surveyor must provide mid-span clearance data and analysis. No such surveyor data is provided.

Decorative lighting may be proposed as part of site landscaping and hardscape (Sheet 31 references exterior lighting requirements). If lighting fixtures are located within clearance distance of overhead electric lines, clearance verification dimensions must be provided showing 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained. No such clearance data is shown.

applicableAreas: southern boundary of site near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) shows trees (labeled as Mitigation and Parking Buffer types) positioned directly on or overlapping the overhead electric line (---OHE---) along the southern property boundary. Plant List (Sheet 35) identifies proposed trees as Cedar Elm (10), Live Oak (2), Mexican Redbud (8), and Texas Mountain Laurel (2). Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors must be from the ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible (UC) list (typically mature height ≤20 feet). No documentation verifies that these species meet the UC compatibility requirement. Landscaping plan must be updated to either relocate trees away from the overhead line or document UC species compliance.

Electric meters are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21). Proposed meter locations must be verified to be unobstructed by site features, structures, fences, or landscaping that would prevent required working clearances (30-inch-wide front space, 36-inch front depth, 6.5-foot headroom). No obstruction verification or detailed meter access details are provided.

applicableAreas: down guy wire anchor points from existing poles in right-of-way
findings.comment: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows down guy wires attached to utility poles in the right-of-way. Guy anchors create ground fixtures that can conflict with proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features. Proposed improvements must verify no conflicts with down guy anchor locations and cables. Site plan does not address or confirm clearance from guy wire anchors, which are frequently omitted from utility records. Conflicts should be resolved through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting poles.

applicableAreas: down guy anchor points from existing distribution poles
findings.comment: Existing distribution poles with down guy wires are shown on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4). Down guy anchor points require dedicated easements 10 feet wide extending minimum 5 feet past where the down guy enters the ground to allow for maintenance and anchor replacement. No easement exhibit documenting these down guy anchor easements is provided or referenced on the site plan.

applicableAreas: construction staging areas and equipment operation zones
findings.comment: Construction will occur on a site with overhead electric lines adjacent to the property. During construction, all staging areas, equipment laydown zones, cranes, material storage, and work platforms must maintain minimum 10-foot radial clearance (all directions) from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA requirements. Erosion Control Plan (Sheet 5) does not document construction staging areas or verify 10-foot working clearance from overhead lines. A Construction Logistics Plan or note on the Erosion Control plan is required.
